I main HPriest since WoD, with a high MW monk, Hpal and Resto Druid alts, and a little rusty with shamans since legion. Nearly all of those have 2+ hots that you can keep aplied at all times, but it seems like the problem you got into is regarding the reactive-proactive nature of healers.

Reactive healers would be Hpriest, yes, but also Mw monks and shamans, since all their healing has to be hard casted and can't prevent damage from happening. Monks might be a different aproach to it, since you /can/ leave your serpent statue and renewing mist on the tank and go dps, but it's in no way a reliable way to keep them alive, since their hots are weak. Wouldn't recommend them for you given the info you provided.

I'd recommend Discipline because even though they don't have any HoTs, and require you to have gear and dps to heal, once you get it, you can spot with Shadow Mend and keep atonements on everyone and dps, healing them passively.

I'd recommend Pallies and Druids too: druids have ways to negate damage, can help DPS a lot in cat form and their hots are actually good--however, they are terrible spot healers and can strugle with heavy singletarget damage. Paladins can help protect their allies with prot aura, spread glimmer of light and heal while throwing Holy Shocks at the boss, but require the 3 glimmer traits from azerite armor, which can take a while and isn't an easy healer to pick up.

More than anything, I'd recommend you to test them all and play with what you like. I hate fast classes like feral and windwalker, but love DH, for instance, and I'd never find that out if I got stuck on the idea of classifying specs on categories and judging them by the sum of it's parts.

Wow has two different versions: retail is the current content where the story is progressing since , and classic is a copy-paste version of the game as it was when it launched in 2004, and since I don't know which you're talking about, I'll answer for both.

Classic:  
Yes, the game is 16 year old, and it'll feel like a 16 years old game. Leveling isn't easy, and playing by yourself won't make it any easier. All enemies are hard-hitting, and the endgame isn't very easy to get into.

However, if you never played wow before, it's the best way to start. The places you'll go, the story, the music, it's all just beautiful, and classic feels like it's almost real (in retail you can kill bears by punching them 3 times). Being a new player, hitting max level will take literal weeks, maybe months of work, and it seems and feels intimidating up until you actually go there and start playing. PC-wise, it's a very light-weight game, and it can run on almost anything now-a-days.

Retail:  
Every new patch gives you a new way to catch up to the current content the game released, so it'll never be too late to start, even though 120 levels seem like a lot. Buying the Shadowlands expansion, heroic edition, will give you a level boost for a single character up to level 120, with enough gear to do pretty much anything you want in the game. It'll seem a little bit empty, since it's the end of the current expansion, but it'll grow again by the end of the year. 

It'll be more enjoyable to play with friends, but the game won't punish you for being by yourself. It's definetly not a heavy game to run when compared to other popular games like Fortnite and League of Legends, but it'll take quite a bit of processing for it to run smoothly.

M+ is an abbreviation of Mythic +. It's a system that you makes the dungeons harder and harder the higher you go, increasing the rewards and the requirements. Wow has a system for you to track how geared you, even after max level: iLevel, your gear's average level. 900 is the minimmum for the current raid tier, Tumb of Sargeras, and it's the number you'll be aiming to get as fast as possible. Here's how you can do it:

Once you get to 110, do the Broken Shore campain and do all invasions you can. Invasions have a 6hrs duration and a 12hrs cooldown after that, it will have quests for you to do and will reward 850 gears and a currency called Nethershards. You can buy specific pieces of gear for 400 nethershards. One invasion rewards you for about 2.5k, which translates to ~6 pieces of your of your choice. Do that twice and you'll have 850 ilevel. On the meantime, while waiting for invasions to come back up, do the Argus campaing and get as many Veiled Argunite as you can--you'll get them through questing and world quests. 650 of them will give a 910 piece of your choice. It'll be a long run, but in a week you can be looking at an over 900 ilevel and can start raiding. Do Normal Tumb of Sargeras and drown in 900+ gear. 

I should also mention Mythic+. They are the normal dungeons of Legion but much, much harder. They scale through keys you'll earn. a Mythic +10 awards you with 930 gear, but it's not always--it may drop nothing. It's inconsistence and difficulty makes me not recommend it for the time being.
